issues.t: Brake booster or booster pump failure
issues.sym: Several warning lights come on at once (brake, ABS, SLIP, master warning), the pedal may feel hard or need much more pressure to stop, and you may hear the pump under the hood buzzing every few seconds. Codes C1391, C1252, C1253 or C1256 are typical.
issues.why: The CT's brakes use an electric pump and pressure accumulator to power the brake booster. Internal leaks in the booster or pump let pressure bleed off, so the pump runs constantly and braking assist can drop. Lexus set up customer support programs (21LE01, and 24LE01 for 2014-2017 cars) that extend coverage on these parts.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Ask a Lexus dealer to check your VIN against programs 21LE01 and 24LE01; 24LE01 covers 10 years or 150,000 miles on eligible 2014-2017 cars.

issues.t: Head gasket leak with rattle and shaking on cold start
issues.sym: A rattle or knock and heavy shaking for the first few seconds after a cold start, misfire codes, a flashing or steady check engine light, coolant going missing, and sometimes white smoke.
issues.why: The 1.8L engine's head gasket can start leaking coolant into a cylinder, often at higher mileage. Owners and shops link it to clogged EGR passages and cooler, and to aging coolant. Left alone, the head can warp and the engine block can be damaged.
issues.next: If the car shakes on start-up or loses coolant, stop using it for long trips and have a cooling system pressure test and combustion leak test done. Early head gasket repair can prevent the need for a replacement engine. Cleaning the EGR system every 50,000-70,000 miles is a common prevention step.

issues.sym: The oil level drops a quart or more between changes with no visible leak; in severe cases a knock or engine damage from running low.
issues.why: Worn piston rings let oil into the combustion chambers where it burns. Owners report dealers pointing to an oil consumption bulletin.
issues.next: Check the dipstick every few fill-ups and top up as needed. Ask a dealer for an oil consumption test and whether any bulletin or goodwill applies.

issues.sym: A check engine light (often code P261B), the temperature gauge rising, or coolant loss. A failed pump can let the engine overheat.
issues.why: The CT's 1.8L engine uses an electric water pump that can wear out. Owners report failures from around 110,000 miles, and one complaint describes a failed pump leading to coolant in a cylinder and a blown head gasket.
issues.next: Don't drive with an overheating warning. Replace the pump with a genuine or OEM-supplier part, since owners report low-quality pumps failing early.

issues.t: Check Hybrid System warning and loss of power
issues.sym: A Check Hybrid System message, a yellow warning triangle and check engine light, and the car limiting speed or refusing to accelerate normally.
issues.why: Faults in the hybrid battery, its cooling fan, the inverter or related sensors can trigger the warning. The hybrid battery cooling fan under the rear seat can clog with dust and pet hair, letting the battery run hot.
issues.next: Have the hybrid codes read by a shop with a hybrid-capable scan tool. Keep the battery cooling fan intake clear and have the fan cleaned during routine service.

issues.t: Exhaust heat recovery valve leaks coolant (service campaign)
issues.sym: The temperature warning and check engine lights come on and the engine can overheat; coolant level drops.
issues.why: The exhaust gas control actuator, which routes exhaust heat to warm the coolant, can leak coolant. Lexus ran a service campaign (CLB) to fix it.
issues.next: Ask a Lexus dealer to check your VIN for campaign CLB. If the engine overheats, stop and have it towed.

issues.sym: A loud bang and the sunroof glass suddenly breaks, often while driving.
issues.why: Owners report the glass panel of the sunroof breaking without being hit.
issues.next: Pull over safely and cover the opening. Report it to NHTSA and ask the dealer about goodwill coverage.

issues.sym: Rough idle, hesitation, misfires on start-up, lower fuel economy, or a check engine light.
issues.why: Oily vapor from the crankcase and carbon from the exhaust build up in the EGR valve, the EGR cooler and the EGR ports in the intake manifold, choking off flow. This buildup is tied to the cold-start shaking and head gasket trouble on this engine.
issues.next: Ask a shop that knows Toyota hybrids to inspect and clean the EGR valve, cooler and intake ports, and replace the PCV valve at the same time.

issues.sym: The car won't go into Ready mode, the dash lights up weakly or not at all, or the key isn't recognized, especially after sitting.
issues.why: The small 12-volt battery that powers the car's computers runs down or wears out; owners report replacing it about every four years.
issues.next: Have the 12-volt battery tested. Jump-starting is done from the terminal under the hood. Replace a weak battery with the correct type.

issues.t: Won't start in very cold weather
issues.sym: On very cold mornings, around 23F or below, the engine won't start or a throttle control code sets.
issues.why: Lexus bulletin LSB-0051-12 traced the problem to the throttle and intake manifold area and released a new manifold assembly.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether bulletin LSB-0051-12 was done on your car.

issues.t: Check engine light with throttle code P2111
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P2111 (throttle stuck open) and a hybrid system code.
issues.why: Lexus issued bulletin L-SB-0061-12 for 2011-2014 CT 200h cars setting these codes.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask a dealer about bulletin L-SB-0061-12.

issues.t: Oil leak from the timing chain area
issues.sym: Oil seeping from the front of the engine around the timing chain cover, with drips under the car.
issues.why: The timing chain cover seal can leak with age. Owners report this as a known issue with a dealer bulletin.
issues.next: Have the leak source confirmed; ask a dealer whether a bulletin or goodwill applies. Keep the oil topped up until repaired.

issues.t: Check engine light from a loose purge or PCV line
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on; the car usually drives normally.
issues.why: A purge and PCV line inside the throttle body housing can separate. Lexus bulletin LSB-0019-15 calls for an engine computer update and a new purge valve.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask a dealer about bulletin LSB-0019-15.

issues.t: Navigation reboots or shows no traffic or weather data
issues.sym: The navigation system restarts after start-up, or traffic and weather features show 'no data available'.
issues.why: Head unit software and data service faults. Owners report this as the most common CT complaint for some years.
issues.next: Ask a dealer for software updates and check the data subscription status.

issues.t: Safety Connect reports the wrong location
issues.sym: Emergency or stolen-vehicle services may show the car in the wrong place.
issues.why: GPS software in the car's data communication module can give an inaccurate location. Lexus ran limited service campaign 19LE05 to update it.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check your VIN for campaign 19LE05; the update may be covered.

issues.sym: The car doesn't unlock or start with the smart key in your pocket.
issues.why: Lexus issued bulletin LSB-0011-12 for an inoperative smart key system on the CT 200h and other models.
issues.next: Try the backup procedure in the owner's manual (hold the key fob to the start button). Replace the fob battery and ask a dealer about the bulletin.
